summary.en: Insert saved keys into a sorted prefix with safe shifts, stable ties and work tied to inversions.
summary.bn: সাজানো অংশে নতুন key ঢুকিয়ে prefix বাড়াও, আর প্রায় সাজানো ডেটার সুবিধা বোঝো।

notes: C17 baseline; general algorithm bounds treat input size as variable.

examples.title: Order five marks, including a tie
examples.explanationHtml: Successive saved keys extend the prefix until it becomes 1 3 3 5 7. The last key 1 shifts four predecessors.

examples.title: Sort numbers entered at the keyboard
examples.explanationHtml: Insertion shifts apply to signed values directly. Strict comparison keeps the two -2 entries in their earlier order.

examples.title: Use sorted neighbours to find distinct marks
examples.explanationHtml: The insertion result places all equal keys together. Counting group beginnings gives three distinct scores.

examples.title: Relate shifts to inversions
examples.explanationHtml: Only pair 3,2 is inverted. One insertion shift removes that inversion, illustrating why almost ordered input is inexpensive.

practice.title: Count predecessor shifts
practice.statementHtml: Count how many predecessor copies shift right during stable insertion sort. After the prompt Enter n, then n values:, read n within 0..64 and n integers within -99..99. Output shifts = S; placing the saved key is not a predecessor shift.
hints: Strictly larger earlier values contribute one shift each.

practice.title: Insert only the requested prefix
practice.statementHtml: Grow an insertion-sorted prefix while leaving the suffix untouched. Print Enter n, then n values: and read n (0..64) plus n values (-99..99); then print Enter prefix length: and read p (0..n). Sort a[0..p) and print the entire resulting row separated by spaces.
hints: Use p as the insertion algorithm length, but n as the displayed row length.

practice.title: Explain the Insertion Sort invariant
practice.statementHtml: For Insertion Sort, state what stays true as the main process repeats. Explain the start, preservation and completed result.
hints: Use the changing boundaries and the processed region in this method.
practice.answerHtml:
Before outer iteration i, a[0..i) is sorted and contains the original first i values. Save the next key. During the inner loop, values shifted to its right are all greater than key and remain in sorted order. When no larger predecessor remains, inserting key at j + 1 creates a sorted prefix of length i + 1.

The outer index grows to n. The inner index decreases until either an ordered predecessor appears or the left boundary is passed. Both loops therefore terminate. Every shift is paired with eventual reinsertion of the saved key, so each completed outer iteration preserves all input records.

practice.title: Derive the resource cost of Insertion Sort
practice.statementHtml: Relate predecessor shifts to the inversion count, including ascending and reverse orders.
hints: Count the work from this algorithm rather than naming a class alone.
practice.answerHtml: Best-case time is Θ(n); reverse-order worst-case time is Θ(n²). For uniformly random distinct permutations, the expected inversion count is n(n - 1)/4, giving quadratic average time. General time is Θ(n + I) for I inversions. Auxiliary storage is Θ(1), and strict shifting preserves stability. These conclusions apply to this insertion routine, not to every algorithm that happens to grow a prefix.

quiz.prompt: Why is key saved before insertion shifts begin?
options: Its original cell may be overwritten
quiz.explanation: Shifting a larger predecessor right can replace a[i].

quiz.prompt: Which guard order protects a negative j?
quiz.explanation: Short-circuit evaluation avoids the array access after j becomes negative.

quiz.prompt: After the inner loop stops at j, where does key belong?
quiz.explanation: The stopped position is the predecessor or the outside-left marker.

quiz.prompt: What determines the number of insertion shifts?
options: The number of equal adjacent pairs
quiz.explanation: Each shift crosses one earlier value greater than the key.

quiz.prompt: Why is ascending input a linear best case?
options: Each new key needs no shift
Every key swaps with the last value
quiz.explanation: There is one failed predecessor test per inserted key.

options: Shift only predecessors strictly greater than key
Shift predecessors equal to key too
quiz.explanation: The new key must stay after earlier equal records.

quiz.prompt: For reverse order, how many shifts can the final key make?
quiz.explanation: The smallest last key passes every earlier value.

quiz.prompt: Where is key 2 placed after shifting the prefix [1,3]?
quiz.explanation: Only 3 shifts; key goes immediately after 1.

quiz.prompt: How many larger predecessors shift for key 1 after [2,3,4]?
quiz.explanation: All three preceding values are larger than 1.

quiz.prompt: Does a predecessor equal to key shift under the strict insertion rule?
quiz.explanation: Equality does not move an earlier record past the new key.

keyPoints.bn: Insertion sort-এ সাজানো prefix ধীরে ধীরে বাড়ে।

keyPoints.bn: a[j] পড়ার আগে বামের সীমা যাচাই করো।

keyPoints.en: Strict shifting preserves the order of ties.
keyPoints.bn: শুধু বড় মান সরালে সমান key-এর ক্রম থাকে।

keyPoints.bn: কাজের পরিমাণ inversion-এর সংখ্যার সঙ্গে বাড়ে।
